stories.headline: Tesla made battery material inside Gigafactory Texas for the first time
Stanford confirms AI swapped a student's race in an official photo
US military used lasers to destroy drones in real combat
India launched its first imaging satellite to geosynchronous orbit
Builder used Grok 4.7 and Blender to model SpaceX Raptor engine in 3D

caption:
Here's what happened in AI and tech in the last 24 hours, from AI swapping a student's face at Stanford to lasers taking down real drones in combat

Tesla produced nickel cathode, a key battery material, inside Gigafactory Texas for the first time.

Stanford confirmed AI was used to replace a student in an official photo with a person of a different race and gender.

The US Pentagon confirmed laser systems destroyed Iranian drones and cruise missiles in the Strait of Hormuz, the Army followed with a $500 million contract for war-ready lasers.

India launched its first satellite that can photograph the entire country from a fixed point in high orbit.

A builder used Grok 4.7 inside Blender to model SpaceX's Raptor engine in 3D, the quality jump from earlier AI versions was immediate, and it's still early.

AI keeps showing up in places most people haven't thought about, faking school photos, shooting down drones, and letting one person model jet engines in 3D. Most of it happened today.
